SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

encourage verb

urge on

also urge, urge on, spur on, encouragement

classical

Quint. 1.10.16: rēmigem cantus hortātur
Traupman 152

hortor, hortārī, hortātus sum

verb, first conjugation, deponent; with ut and the subjunctive, or ad and the accusative

encourage, urge

In poetry also with an infinitive: hortāturque sequī (Ov. Met. 8.215).

Other words

  • adhortor, adhortārī, adhortātus sum — encourage, urge on

    verb, first conjugation, deponent; with ad and the accusative, or ut and the subjunctive · also used · classical · Cic. Rab. Perd. 1 (Lewis & Short): mē meae vītae cōnsuētūdō ad C. Rabīrium dēfendendum est adhortāta; Traupman 309

  • cohortor, cohortārī, cohortātus sum — encourage (a group), rally

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.25 (Lewis & Short): cohortātus suōs proelium commīsit

    Lewis & Short: “to animate or encourage by forcible language … esp., of the general before a battle”.

  • hortātiō, hortātiōnis f. — encouragement

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 9.14.7 (Lewis & Short): hortātiō nōn est necessāria

    Traupman (152, 309) gives hortātus.

Examples

  • velut āles, ab altō quae teneram prōlem prōdūxit in āera nīdō, hortāturque sequī

    like a bird that has led her tender young out of the high nest into the air, and urges them to followOv. Met. 8.213–215

  • sī quidem et rēmigem cantus hortātur

    for song spurs on even the rowerQuint. 1.10.16

  • Hortātus est mē ut Latīnē loquerer.

    He encouraged me to speak Latin.composed

See also encourage, well done.

SourcesLewis & Short: hortor · Lewis & Short: adhortor · Lewis & Short: cohortor · Lewis & Short: hortatio

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 152, 309, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).

Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-ovidius, loci-quintilianus), checked against the editions named there.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
